2. It appears from the order-sheet that after the filing of the suit, the plaintiff also filed a petition for temporary inquisition for restraining the defendants (opposite parties Nos. 1-5 and 7 and 8) from transferring the suit land to anybody pending disposal of the suit and by order dated 24-1-80, an ad interim order of injunction was passed. Urgent processes were issued for the service of notice and also the writ of injunction by order dated 28-1-80. From the order dated 12-2-80, it appears that the summons were served on the defendants and defendants Nos. 2 and 3 i.e opposite-parties Nos. 8 and 5 respectively, appeared and prayed for time to tile written statement and written objection. The prayer was allowed and 3-4-80 was fixed for filing written statement and written objection. From order dated 3-4-80, it appears that the writ of injunction was served and Mr. Jasir Ali, Advocate (opposite party No. 6) was appointed Court Guardian for the minor defend Nos. 4.7 i.e. opposite-party Nos. 1.4 Defendant Nos. 2 and 3 also prayed for time on that date, for filing written statement and-written objection and the prayers were allowed and the suit was fixed on 22-5-80 In the mean-time, the court guardian submitted his report on 5-5-80. Ultimately, the defendants did not submit any when statement or written objection in the suit Defendant Nos. 1 and 2 compromised the suit with the plaintiff petitioner and the suit was decreed on compromise against them and ex-parte against the rest by order dated 29-9-80. 

 3. After the decree, the plaintiff filed Title Execution Case No. 16 of 1980 and obtained a kabala from opposite-party Nos. 1-5 through court. 

 4. On 15-5-81 one Alauddin Chowdhury, representing himself as paternal uncle of the minor opposite parties, filed a petition under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure praying for setting-aside the decree passed on 29-9-80 against the minors, alleging that no notice of the suit was served on the minors. The learned Sub-ordinate Judge, fixing 20-5-81 for hearing the matter in presence of both the sides and on that date, he passed the impugned order, setting-aside the ex-parte decree, so far it relates to minor defendants. On the same date, the learned sub-ordinate Judge, also stayed Title Examination Case No. 16/80 and recalled the kabala from the Registry Office, if not registered. In the meantime the kabala was registered on 1-4-81. 

 5. Being aggrieved, the plaintiff-petitioner preferred Civil Revision No. 1170 of 1981 against the order setting-aside the ex parte decree and Civil Revision No 1169 of 1981 against the order staying Title Execution Case No. 16 1483, recalling the kabala. 

 6. The learned Advocate Mr. Dewan A, MS Zaman for the petitioners, has taken me through the petitions and other papers on record. He contends that as there are alternative remedies for setting-aside the ex-parte decree, under Order 9, rule 13, Civil Procedure Code, and also provision for appeal as well under section 96 of the same Code, the learned Sub-ordinate Judge was not justified in setting aside the decree and making the impugned orders under section 151 CPC In support of his contention, he relied on the cases of Uzarichula Buzfuz vs Syed Jelea Begum, reported in 22 DLR 383, Azizur Rahman vs Janata Bank reported in 28 DLR 252, and Punjab Ali Pk vs Md. Mukaram Hossain, reported in 29 DLR (SC) 188. In the first case it was observed as follows. 

 In the second and third cases, similar decisions were made. The law is quite well settled that the powers under section 151 cannot be exercised when there are alternative remedies to the parties seeking relief. So it is evident that the impugned order of the learned Sub-ordinate Judge, setting-aside the ex-parte decree under section 151 CP Code against the minor opposite-parties is totally without jurisdiction and illegal. 

 So far the impugned order of the Civil Revision No. 1169 of 1981, it is evidence that the order was made after the execution of the decree, when the court becomes functus officio and that order also is without jurisdiction. In this confection, the learned Advocate for the petitioner Mr Zaman has referred to the case of Abdul Hakim and another vs Guleda Begum and another reported in BLD 1984, at page 55, where it was held that the executing court becomes functus officio after execution of the decree. The learned Advocate Mr Nurul Huda Jaigirder for opposite-party Nos. 1-4, has got no reply to the above legal position.
